title: Ordinary roots and reciprocal roots
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and let
$k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$,
and choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0/k_0$
be smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq0}$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, fix an indeterminate $T$, and, for
every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, set $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, the
ordinary cohomology group, and let $F_{i,\ell}$ be the geometric-Frobenius
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed] operator on this space, and set
$P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$ to be the determinant
family in the smooth-proper cohomological family
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]. All roots are taken in this
chosen algebraically closed field $\Qlb$.

Let $P(T)\in\Ql[T]$ be a polynomial with $P(0)=1$. An *ordinary root* is a
scalar $\beta\in\Qlb$ satisfying $P(\beta)=0$. It is nonzero. A *reciprocal
root* is a scalar $\alpha\in\Qlb^\times$ satisfying $P(\alpha^{-1})=0$. Over
an algebraic closure one has

$$
 P(T)=\prod_j(1-\alpha_jT),
$$

where the $\alpha_j$, counted with algebraic multiplicity, are the reciprocal
roots.

mathlib_searches.verdict: no match for the definition as a whole, which is tied to the family P_{i,ℓ} = det(1 - T F_{i,ℓ} | H^i(X, Q_ℓ)) that Mathlib does not have; its ingredients are leaves: an ordinary root of P in Qlb is Polynomial.IsRoot (P.map ι) β (def-weil-polynomial-root), a reciprocal root α is a root of Polynomial.reverse P, equivalently (eval₂_reverse_eq_zero_iff) a nonzero α with P(α⁻¹) = 0, and the multiplicity is Polynomial.rootMultiplicity (def-weil-root-multiplicity); the factorization asserted in the last sentence is the new node lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against its source (master blueprint, order 2859): verbatim, kept; the slopmaster2 blueprint has no copy of this node and no Lean exists on either branch. The first paragraph only restates the setting of def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family; the definition proper is the second paragraph, about a polynomial P in Q_l[T] with P(0)=1. Kept the five imported statement dependencies, each verified to supply something the statement uses: the datum p,a,q,k_0,k, the prime l, Q_l and the chosen algebraic closure Qlb (def-weil-finite-field-fiber); smooth, proper, geometrically connected, pure dimension d (def-weil-geometric-hypotheses); the geometric-Frobenius convention, cited in the text (def-weil-frobenius-detailed); H^i(X,Q_l) (def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology); V_{i,l}, F_{i,l} and P_{i,l} (def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family). Added the notions the second paragraph is built from: 'algebraically closed field' and 'algebraic closure' for Qlb (existing leaf def-weil-algebraic-closure, in sec-nagata-compactification); the polynomial ring Q_l[T] and the constant coefficient P(0) (existing leaf def-weil-polynomial-ring); the evaluation P(beta) of a polynomial over Q_l at a point of Qlb and the notion of root in an extension field, which the DAG lacked (new leaf def-weil-polynomial-root, Polynomial.eval₂ / Polynomial.IsRoot); 'algebraic multiplicity' (existing leaf def-weil-root-multiplicity, Polynomial.rootMultiplicity). The sentences 'It is nonzero' and 'Over an algebraic closure one has P(T)=prod_j(1-alpha_j T), where the alpha_j, counted with algebraic multiplicity, are the reciprocal roots' are assertions, not part of the definition, and the multiplicity of a reciprocal root is not defined by the text: they are stated as the new node lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization (unsplit; Mathlib has the ingredients Splits.eq_prod_roots, IsAlgClosed.splits_domain, count_roots, eval₂_reverse_eq_zero_iff but not the statement), which fixes the multiplicity of a reciprocal root alpha as the multiplicity of alpha^{-1} as a root of P, equivalently of alpha as a root of the reciprocal polynomial of lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial. Recorded a Mathlib search for the item itself: no match for the definition as a whole; its ingredients are leaves.
